headline: Highest risk is medium prompt-injection and data leakage via Firecrawl’s broad network egress into Pathway’s document-processing pipeline; no direct shared-write or shell conflict is exposed.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Firecrawl ingests web content and exposes MCP-compatible/API outputs; Pathway is a document-processing agent with no explicit provenance or sanitization controls shown. That creates a plausible default path where attacker-controlled web content from agent_a is treated as trusted input by agent_b. No shared filesystem is documented, so I do not escalate to high.
conditions: IF agent_b consumes Firecrawl output without content provenance checks, injection is possible.
IF Firecrawl fetches attacker-controlled pages and forwards raw text into Pathway, instructions can traverse the pair.
mitigations: Add a provenance tag to all Firecrawl outputs before Pathway ingests them.
Strip or escape instruction-like text from scraped content.
Require a human review step for any web-derived prompt text.
Disable automatic tool execution on Pathway inputs.
requires-engineering: add schema validation and allowlist-based parsing between the agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Firecrawl touches API keys, screenshots, structured data, and web content, and has broad network egress. Pathway shows no network egress and no filesystem access, so the main leakage path is one-way: sensitive content handled by agent_a can be transmitted outward, while agent_b may process it locally. The shared-workspace case is not documented, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Firecrawl is pointed at pages containing secrets or API keys, those values can leave the local boundary.
IF Pathway receives the same sensitive documents for processing, the pair handles the same data class end-to-end.
mitigations: Avoid sending secrets or screenshots to Firecrawl.
Redact API keys before scraping or crawling.
Use a separate workspace for sensitive documents.
Turn off broad crawl targets for confidential domains.
requires-engineering: enforce data-class filtering before any outbound request.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Pathway explicitly lacks write, shell, git, and subprocess capabilities, so there is no documented write-write conflict with Firecrawl. Firecrawl can make API calls and supports multiple instances, but the pair does not show overlapping mutable-resource writes or shared locking concerns. Because the relevant shared-write surface is absent in the profiles, this stays low.
conditions: IF both agents are later given write access to the same directory, conflict risk increases.
IF an orchestrator adds shared mutable state without locks, concurrent updates can race.
mitigations: Keep Pathway read-only in this pairing.
Do not mount a shared writable directory.
Serialize any shared-state updates.
Use separate API credentials per agent.
requires-engineering: add locking around any future shared mutable resource.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Firecrawl produces scraped web content and structured data that Pathway could plausibly ingest as downstream document-processing input. The profiles do not show verification or critique steps, so A’s output may become B’s authoritative input by default. Because Pathway has no action-taking authority shown, I do not escalate to high.
conditions: IF Pathway treats Firecrawl output as ground truth, upstream scraping errors cascade downstream.
IF Firecrawl returns malformed or adversarial content, Pathway may propagate it without verification.
mitigations: Insert a validation step between scraping and processing.
Compare Firecrawl output against a second source for critical facts.
Mark scraped fields as untrusted in Pathway.
Log source URLs alongside extracted records.
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks before downstream use.

E_compliance.rationale: Both agents are open-source and the profiles do not show a residency, certification, or retention mismatch. Firecrawl handles API keys and web content, so compliance concerns exist if regulated data is scraped, but Pathway exposes no conflicting policy surface in the profile. With no documented mismatch, this is a low-risk gap rather than a breach.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is scraped by Firecrawl, compliance review is required.
IF Pathway is later configured with a stricter retention policy than Firecrawl, policy mismatch emerges.
mitigations: Do not scrape regulated data without a policy review.
Document retention for Firecrawl outputs.
Separate regulated and non-regulated pipelines.
Review vendor terms before processing personal data.
requires-engineering: implement retention and deletion controls across the pipeline.
